description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
One attention layer (d80, 1 head). Query at answer step k attends to fixed prompt position PERM[k] via position one-hots; value copies the token one-hot into a separate block read by the head.
Same circuit as PosPermCopy-d80-1L but all LayerNorms replaced by identity (GAIN=20 so the attention stays near-hard). Tests whether LN is needed at all.
PosPermCopy-noLN with the MLP removed (d_ff=0, Block skips it). The circuit is now only embeddings + one attention head + a linear read-out.
PosPermCopy-noLN-noMLP with token and copied-token identities encoded as 5-bit +-1 codes instead of one-hots (d_model 80 -> 33). Head reads <code_c, copied bits>, exact argmax.
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=0.5 (attention nearly uniform over prompt).
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=1.0 (attention still nearly uniform).
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=2.0.
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=3.0.
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=5.0.
Gain sweep on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33: GAIN=4.0.
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): query weights zeroed for answer steps 0-2 (the first copied word).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): query weights zeroed for answer steps 3-7 (separator and middle word).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): query weights zeroed for answer steps 8-10 (the last copied word).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): all query weights zeroed (attention becomes uniform over the prefix).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): all key weights zeroed (every key scores 0, so attention is uniform over the prefix).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): all value weights zeroed (attention still selects correctly but carries no token information).
Ablation on PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 (GAIN=5): output projection W_o zeroed (attention copies nothing into the residual).
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with the copied-token block placed on top of the token block (CPY=TOK=0). Tests whether a separate copy subspace is needed.
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with the causal mask removed from attention (queries see future positions too). Tests whether the circuit relies on causality.
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with a second, all-zero block appended (n_layers=2). Residual pass-through, so depth should not change the result.
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with d_model padded to 64 (unused dims are all zero). Checks that unused residual width is inert.
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with an 8-wide MLP present but all-zero (d_ff=8). Checks that an idle MLP is inert.
PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with LayerNorm restored (ln1, ln2, final_ln; gains 1, biases 0, no MLP). Checks whether normalization breaks the exact copy.
LN version of PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with GAIN=6.0 (gain sweep under LayerNorm).
LN version of PosPermCopy-BitCode-d33 with GAIN=4.0 (gain sweep under LayerNorm).
LN version (GAIN=5) with 0/1 bit codes instead of +-1 for token and copied-token codes. Tests whether the +-1 sign convention is necessary for the head's argmax.
LN version (GAIN=5, +-1 codes) with the bit order reversed in the token and head codes. Checks that the particular code assignment is arbitrary.
LN version with PERM = identity (copy the prompt in place). Control: the task's word reversal must come from PERM, not from the weights' code assignment.
LN version (GAIN=5, standard codes) with the position one-hot scaled to 0.5. Checks how the scale of the position embedding interacts with the gain.
LN version (GAIN=5, standard codes) with the position one-hot scaled to 2.0. Checks how the scale of the position embedding interacts with the gain.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0) with GAIN=3.0. Gain sweep under LayerNorm, lower end.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0) with GAIN=2.0. Gain sweep under LayerNorm, lower end.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0) with GAIN=1.0. Gain sweep under LayerNorm, lower end.
LN version (GAIN=5) with token and copied-token codes scaled to +-2 (token emb and head). Checks that the magnitude of the codes does not matter, only the argmax.
LN version (GAIN=5, standard codes) with the read-out head scaled by 0.1. Logits shrink uniformly, so argmax (and accuracy) should be unchanged.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0, head scale 1.0) with GAIN=10.0. Upper end of the gain sweep under LayerNorm.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0, head scale 1.0) with GAIN=20.0. Upper end of the gain sweep under LayerNorm.
LN version (standard codes, position scale 1.0, head scale 1.0) with GAIN=50.0. Last point of the gain sweep under LayerNorm.
No-LayerNorm version (GAIN=5, no MLP) with 0/1 bit codes for token and copied-token codes. Checks whether the 0/1 result seen with LayerNorm also holds without it.
